preferred: Hillier & Marshall (1992) — Organic maturation… Orcadian Basin; J. Geol. Soc. London 149, 491–502.

Pirrie, D., Bevins, R.E., Ixer, R.A., Pearce, N.J.G., Turner, P., Power, M.R. et al. (2026) — Searching for the origin of the Stonehenge Altar Stone: new sedimentological, petrographical, mineralogical, geochemical and isotopic constraints; J. Geol. Soc. 183, jgs2026-090, doi:10.1144/jgs2026-090 (https://www.lyellcollection.org/doi/full/10.1144/jgs2026-090); dataset doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.33993488.v1.
also: Hillier & Clayton (1989) — Illite/smectite diagenesis vs organic maturity; Clay Minerals 24, 181–196.
Barker & Pawlewicz (1986) — Ro ↔ maximum palaeotemperature calibration.
Daw, T. (2026) — The Altar Stone – Maybe Not The Orcadian Basin?; sarsen.org, 11 Jul 2026.
sets.supplies: Coastal Ro from Hillier & Marshall 1992 Figs 2–4, contrasted with the Altar Stone's ~20%-expandable I/S vs <10% in Caithness and Orkney (Pirrie et al. 2026). The stone's Ro is not measured; the ≲1% Ro-equivalent is Daw's inference (sarsen.org, 11 Jul 2026), not a figure from Bevins et al. or Pirrie et al.

sets.title: Strontium: Sr ceiling (L10) and Sr/Ca (L11)
preferred: Rochelle, Bateman, Milodowski, Pearce & Savage (1990) — BGS Technical Report WE/90/35 (Nirex NSS/R246), Table 5: whole-rock XRF, Caithness Flagstone CS037P, Castletown Quarry.

Phillips (2002) — A review of petrological data available for the Reay District and adjacent areas, Caithness; BGS Internal Report IR/02/074, Appendix 1 (Dounreay Borehole 1; data from Ingham et al. 1991 and Hyslop & Milodowski 1994, Nirex Report 639).
Bevins et al. (2024) — Stones of Stenness/Ring of Brodgar pXRF geochemistry (§5.4, Figs. 8–10); J. Archaeol. Sci. Rep. 58, 104738.
Daw, T. (2026) — Don’t Judge The Altar Stone By Its Cover; sarsen.org, 5 Sep 2026 (Altar Stone pXRF Sr and Ca by chip).
also: Bevins et al. (2022) — Linking derived debitage to the Stonehenge Altar Stone using portable X-ray fluorescence analysis; Mineralogical Magazine 86, 688–700 (doi:10.1180/mgm.2022.22).
sets.supplies: Altar Stone pXRF Sr 53–156 ppm (Bevins et al. 2022 analyses plus the 2022 dry-surface set; chip means 114–125 ppm in the 5 Sep 2026 post) and Sr/Ca ~1.1–1.6×10⁻³ (chips 2010K.240 and FN593). Castletown CS037P Sr 406 ppm, CaO 7.37% (lab XRF). Dounreay BH1 flagstones Sr median 415 ppm (131–1388, n = 29; lab XRF). Orkney: Yesnaby body 220–700 ppm; Stenness/Brodgar stones ~400 to 1260 ppm (pXRF). Caveat: handheld pXRF on the Altar Stone vs lab XRF on Caithness rock; the Sr/Ca rests on three chips; untested is not a fail.
